title: Linear equations
examples: Teacher, what is the balance method?
If I have variables on both sides, how do I start?
Can you show me how to deal with brackets in an equation?

explain.say: Today we learn to solve linear equations using the balance method. We keep both sides equal always.
To keep the balance, whatever you do on one side you must do on the other. If we subtract three from the left we must subtract three from the right.
Next we look at unknowns on both sides. We want to gather all the x terms on one side. Let us subtract two x from both sides.
Now we deal with brackets. Remember to multiply the number outside by every term inside the brackets. For example, two times the bracket gives two times each term.
Let us solve five x minus three equals two x plus nine. First we move the x terms together. Subtract two x from both sides to begin.

faq.q: What does 'balance method' really mean when solving equations?
faq.a: It means that the equation is like a seesaw. Whatever you take away or add to one side you must do to the other side to keep it balanced.
asks: How do I keep the equation balanced?
What is the rule for keeping it equal?

faq.q: If I have variables on both sides, which side should I move them to?
faq.a: It is usually easiest to move the variable term to the side that keeps the coefficient positive. This helps avoid negative signs.
asks: Do I move x to the left or right?
Which side is better for the unknowns?

faq.q: When I see brackets, do I just multiply the outside number by the first term?
faq.a: No, you must multiply the number outside the brackets by every single term inside the brackets. You must distribute it fully.
asks: Do I only multiply the first term in the brackets?

faq.q: Can I move a number from one side to the other by changing its sign?
faq.a: Yes, this is a shortcut for adding or subtracting. If you move a term across the equals sign, you change its sign.
asks: If I move a number, what happens to it?
Is changing the sign the same as adding?

faq.q: What if I have brackets and unknowns on both sides?
faq.a: First, expand all the brackets completely. Then, follow the steps for unknowns on both sides to solve the resulting equation.
asks: What order should I solve in?
Do I expand first or move the variables first?

facts: An equation shows that two expressions are equal in value.
To solve an equation, you must isolate the unknown variable on one side.
When moving a term across the equals sign, you change its sign.
The balance method ensures that the equation remains true throughout the solving process.

quiz.why: We subtract two x from both sides to get two x plus five equals eleven. Then we subtract five from both sides to get two x equals six, so x is three.

wrong.0: This mistake occurs if you incorrectly subtract 2x from 4x and then subtract 5 from 11, leaving you with 2x = 6.
wrong.1: This mistake is tempting because you might add the numbers together instead of subtracting the variables.
wrong.3: This mistake happens because you only subtract the 2x from the 4x and forget to subtract it from the 5 on the left side.

quiz.why: First, expand the brackets to get three y minus three equals y plus five. Then, subtract y from both sides to get two three y minus three equals five, so three y equals eight, and y is four.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you only multiply the 3 by the y inside the bracket and forget to multiply the 3 by the minus one.
wrong.2: This mistake occurs if you incorrectly move the 3y to the right side and subtract it from the other y.
wrong.3: This mistake is tempting because you might incorrectly add the 3 to the 5 on the right side.

quiz.why: We want the unknowns on the left, so we subtract five k from both sides. This gives negative three k plus seven equals minus two. Then we subtract seven from both sides to get negative three k equals minus nine, so k is three.

wrong.0: This mistake occurs if you only balance the constants and ignore the variables entirely.
wrong.1: This mistake is tempting because you might add the 7 and the 2 together instead of subtracting them.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you incorrectly move the 7 to the right side and add it to the minus two.
